main_text.p: ulla deflectione possunt, Audi nos benigne[?] Pater, & pro omnipotenti tua bonitate concede, ut ita benedicas & sanctifices verbo tuo, & spiritu tuo sancto hæc tua dona, has tuas creaturas panis & vini, ut sint nobis corpus & sanguis dilecti filii tui, &c. quæ sunt formalia verba Canonis Missæ. In eadem precatione margini apponuntur hæc, Presbyter officiaris sumet seu tollat patinam in manus, dum hoc est corpus meum repetitur, & calicem, dum dicitur hic est sanguis novi Testamenti, finita consecratione immediatè subjungitur memoriale, seu oratio oblationis (quæ in missali Romano vocatur oblatio rememorativa) in qua dicitur, Christum voluisse nos illud memoriale celebrare in memoriam, non solum beatæ passionis, sed & potentis resurrectionis, gloriosæ ascensionis, &c. &, ut verbo dicam, quantum declinat hic liber ab Anglico, tanto propius accedit ad missale Romanum, plurimas alias mutationes in deterius observarunt Scoti, & profitentur apertè, se probaturos omnes materiales partes canonis missæ, seminaliter ibi positas, & parvo temporis intervallo missam posse inde fabricari.

Sed redeo ad narrationem, defunctus necessaria hac excursione, quia librorum horum in sequentibus frequentissima futura est mentio, utpote, quod omnibus hisce dissidiis causam dederint, Episcopis omni conatu urgentibus, ut ab Ecclesiis reciperentur, nullo præeunte Synodi Nationalis examine aut judicio, cujus consensum se nunquam obtenturos sciebant, itaque denuo, ad supremum Regis senatum confugiunt, cujus mandato omnes jubentur regio mandato parere, cum certificatione (ut ita loquar) nisi in usum Parœciarum singuli Pastores duo exemplaria comparent, se interdicturos eis aqua & igni, rebelliumque poenas non evasuros. Interim vero quidam Episcoporum, non expectato die à Rege præfinito (Paschatis festo) statim ea li-tur.

page.notes: The printed text is set in a single column. A printed mark (an asterisk-like sign) stands at the start of the paragraph beginning "Sed redeo"; it is not transcribed as text. The running head is partly covered by a library stamp and the word after "SCOTI" is unclear; the final letter is read as Æ with doubt. "benigne" is partly obscured by a stamp at the top of the page. Faint dashes and the letters "ex" at the far right edge near the bottom are edge marks or show-through, not margin notes, and are not transcribed. A stray mark at the lower left is not text. The word "tur." at the foot of the text is the completion of "litur" broken across lines, so it is treated as part of the final paragraph and not as a catchword.
